name: CA-31
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's 8-point Democratic lean plus a favorable national environment
Cisneros holds a large fundraising advantage over Eric Ching
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Cisneros: an 8-point Democratic district, a favorable environment, incumbency, and a roughly 7-to-1 fundraising edge, with markets also pricing him near certain. With no contrary polling or ratings, the forecast stays at a Safe D margin near 20 points.
model.watch: Any late public polling or a surge of outside spending against Cisneros would be the first sign the margin is narrowing.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Incumbent Democrat Gil Cisneros is seeking another term in a Southern California district that leans Democratic by about eight points. He advanced to the general election and has heavily out-raised Republican Eric Ching, who has raised under $100,000 and has little cash on hand. Outside spending in the race has been minimal so far.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive. Prediction markets give Cisneros roughly a 96% chance of winning. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the fundraising gap points to a comfortable Democratic win, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any specific evidence of a competitive race.
